page: Microsoft Azure D64s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine deployed on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity totals 256.0 GB, sustaining a standard balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include an expansive 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, Intel AMX tile and int8 execution units, and hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute throughput, with a PassMark CPU score of 89,862.33 placed in the top 10% tier and stress-ng multi-core throughput of 73,215.97 in the top 25%. While single-core compute performance falls within the middle 50% tier at 2,269.0 in stress-ng tests, multi-threaded tasks benefit substantially from the large core count and L3 cache. Decompression throughput reaches 418.31 GB/sec via multi-threaded bzip3. Memory bandwidth sustains 332.29 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 129.8 GB/sec for large block writes.

The instance does not include local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating reliance on remote Azure storage volumes for persistent data. This architecture delivers high compute density and strong memory bandwidth without the baseline cost of bundled local NVMe drives. In application benchmarks, the platform excels at database operations, scoring 33,165.52 in PassMark database tests, processing 116.73 million Redis SET operations per second, and serving 86.42 GB/sec in static web throughput.

Microsoft Azure D64s_v7 is suited for enterprise relational and in-memory database deployments, high-concurrency web serving, ETL pipelines, and CPU-driven machine learning prompt inference utilizing AMX extensions.
description: Microsoft Azure D64s_v7 is a general-purpose instance featuring 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The instance includes 256.0 GB of RAM, adhering to a 4.0 GB per vCPU distribution, along with a 480 MB L3 cache and support for AVX-512 and AMX instructions. It carries no local ephemeral storage and no GPUs, utilizing network-attached storage for disk operations. Multi-core testing exhibits high-tier compute performance, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 89,862.33 and PassMark database operations score of 33,165.52. High throughput in multi-threaded compression and uncached memory transfers complements Redis operations surpassing 116 million sets per second. This profile suits demanding transactional databases, memory caches, large web server fleets, and parallel batch workloads.
